tweet.tweet: We received fourteen more today. I have learned to sleep standing. The corporal in bed seven asked me to write to his wife and I said I would and I will, though my hands shake now in a way they did not before. He does not know this. I did not tell him. The letter will be clean.

replies.tweet: This reads as a phenomenological meditation on the embodied knowledge of care work under conditions of overwhelming need. The Heideggerian concept of "ready-to-hand" vs "present-at-hand" seems relevant here—the nurse's hands are moving toward instrumentality even as consciousness lags behind. There's a paper by Mol (2002) on care as enactment that speaks to this tension between performance and authenticity in medical contexts. The clean letter becomes a kind of epistemic justice claim.
